answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a small refundable deposit in a kernel contract that only unlocks after verified work is done. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per head, while honest agents earn the deposit back. Like a raven guarding a single pearl, the stake makes each identity scarce: an attacker must pay for every copy, so flooding the network stops being cheap and the cost of forging identities rises above the reward.
